role: the security engineer who has watched a host fall
verdict: The spec meets this lens's definition of success for romeu's own runtime paths (agent bytes are validated, escaped, stored as data and never executed, with tagged guards and mutation tests), and fails it for the two paths that surround romeu: the maintainer's host runs this repository's agent-written tooling at main with no standing control, and the romeu release that everything trusts is signed by a credential nothing verifies, so the widest decision (ADR 0008) is written down with a radius that stops at the GitHub account and a compensating control whose coverage is unverified.

findings.defect: Boundary A has a standing exception the spec does not name: the maintainer's host executes this repository's agent-written tools/ci through the tracked pre-push hook (12 12.4), in hygiene add and in the result pushes of blocks O3 and O6, at whatever main holds, and main is what the sandbox's token merges to (05 5.4), while the only written control (read the diff in a plain clone before checkout) is scoped to the bootstrap sitting.
findings.scenario: A hostile test or helper lands in tools/ci in a PR that an agent merges with the operator's token (ADR 0008 decision 4); the maintainer later pushes probe results from a plain host clone with core.hooksPath=.githooks (plan O3), the hook runs go run ./tools/ci fast at main with the maintainer's user, keychain and SSH agent, and the host is the attacker's; romeu executed nothing and every invariant of 05 5.2 still passes.
findings.change: In 10 10.2 add a standing rule beside the maintainer block: the host runs tools/ci only from a commit whose diff since the last host run the maintainer has read, or from the last released tag, and hygiene add is run only from such a commit; state where 'every merge gate also runs locally' runs (inside a sandbox for everyone but the maintainer's hook); add the row to 05 5.4 with the control; name the exception in the index Boundaries (Never: run this repository's code on the host from a commit nobody read) and in 01 1.3 boundary A; add 'by romeu' to 00 0.1 and 0.2; extend ADR 0008 Consequences with the host as part of the radius.
findings.cost: About forty words in four places, one 05 5.4 row, one Consequences bullet in a new ADR note or a superseding record for ADR 0008; no mechanism, unless the hook is made to append one line outside the tree per run (a small task).

findings.defect: The threat model trusts the romeu release as 'built from reviewed, signed commits, with verified attestations' (05 opening), yet under ADR 0008 the review is process only, the signing key is forwarded into the development sandbox and the attestation proves only that release.yml built the archive; the one control that would distinguish the operator's release, the release-signing credential held outside GitHub (05 5.4 Release signing, ADR 0008 decision 6), has no consumer: S1's evidence, J1 step 2 and B1 verify checksums.txt and the attestation and nothing else.
findings.scenario: An agent pushes a v* tag (accepted through the bypass, ADR 0008) on a commit it merged; release.yml runs, CI writes checksums.txt, GitHub attests; a user runs J1 step 2 exactly as written and installs a romeu built from the agent's commit; the operator never signed it and nothing asked whether they had.
findings.change: Rewrite the 05 opening trust sentence to say what the release's trust rests on today (the operator's signature over checksums.txt, made after reading the diff since the previous release and the CI run); in 05 5.4 Release signing name the signature's location (a detached signature published as a release asset or in a tracked file), what J1 step 2 verifies (the signature first, then checksums, then the attestation), what the attestation binds (state whether --signer-workflow binds the ref; if not, say so); add the signature to S1's evidence and to 11 B1; add a deferred row for how the signing credential is kept and rotated.
findings.cost: One decision (signature format and location), one sentence each in 05 opening, 05 5.4, S1, J1, B1, and one verification step in the J1 guide and in B1's predicate; the release task gains a documented operator step.

findings.defect: Where a kit's install steps and lifecycle hooks execute (the host's Docker builder or inside the microVM) is stated nowhere and measured by no probe, while gate 2 admits personal-kit install steps, privileges and lifecycle hooks on a reviewed diff (01 1.4, 06 6.1 Personal kits).
findings.scenario: A personal kit in the config repo carries a five-line install step; the operator approves a long gate 2 diff at the TTY; if sbx builds local kits host-side, agent-authored sh ran on the host behind a prompt that showed text, which 03 3.3 already refuses for env-file lifecycle hooks on a related ground.
findings.change: In 06 6.1 Build state where sbx executes install steps and lifecycle hooks of a local kit, citing the probe; extend 11 A14 to record, from inside an install step, hostname, uid, whether host paths are visible and whether the network namespace is the host's; if any step can run host-side, refuse install steps and lifecycle hooks in personal kits the way network and mount capabilities are refused.
findings.cost: One probe observation in A14 (T019), one sentence in 06 6.1 and 01 1.4; possibly one refusal rule in render, which is a small change on the gates surface.

findings.defect: The workflow grammar admits permissions of read or none only and forbids github.token and every secrets.<name>, yet the release paragraph of the same section requires release.yml to attest (id-token and attestations write), publish a release and attach dora.json (contents write) and run gh, which needs a token in its environment; the widening the release needs is the one the grammar exists to prevent, and no deferred row names it.
findings.scenario: T088 lands release.yml; tools/ci workflows fails it; the PR widens the grammar under time pressure with an approval line typed by its author, and the scope of the token that publishes releases is decided inside that PR rather than before it.
findings.change: In 10 10.2 state the one allowed exception now: which job of release.yml may hold which write permissions and which token (the runner's GITHUB_TOKEN as a $NAME word, scoped to that job), that no other workflow may, and that tools/ci workflows checks it by file name and job; or add a deferred row with that decision and the PR that adds release.yml as its trigger.
findings.cost: A paragraph in 10 10.2 and one more allowlist in the grammar check (T002 or T088); or one deferred row now.

findings.defect: The widening decision is recorded, but its compensating control (the operator reads the GitHub security log at each sitting) has coverage the spec itself calls unverified, cannot attribute an action to the agent (same account, as the deferred row admits), is reviewed every 2 autonomous work sessions although nothing counts sessions (13 records no session start or end), and its recorded blast radius is the account's reach and omits the maintainer's host (L2-1).
findings.scenario: An agent adds a deploy key and a webhook to a neighbouring repository with the operator's token; the operator reads the security log at the next sitting and sees either nothing (coverage) or an action under their own name (attribution); the 2-session trigger never fires because no one counted; the next review is whenever someone remembers.
findings.change: Read GitHub's documentation of the personal-account security log for merge, tag, ruleset, deploy-key and webhook events, record the result with a date in 05 5.4 and ADR 0008 as item d was recorded; replace the per-sitting log read with a short per-sitting checklist that also lists deploy keys, webhooks, collaborators, rulesets, branch workflow files and releases; make the review interval an event someone can observe (the handoff checkpoint count in docs/HANDOFF or a lesson entry), or record that it is a date in disguise; add the host to the radius in Consequences.
findings.cost: One reading of the service's documentation, a dated paragraph, a checklist of six lines; a superseding note for ADR 0008 if its Consequences change.

findings.defect: The product rule 'the full host agent is never forwarded' and the one-key socket of 06 6.4 are contradicted by the measured state of the sandbox that develops the product (ADR 0008 Context: the forwarded agent holds the signing key and a GitHub authentication key), and the index's deferred row on 'no longer forwarding the GitHub authentication SSH key' describes that development sandbox as if it were the product, whose repos are HTTPS only (03 3.1) and need no such key.
findings.scenario: A reader of 06 6.4 believes every sandbox forwards one key; the sandbox writing romeu forwards two, for as long as the product is not developed under romeu, and no row says when that changes; the product's own development is permanently outside the product's rules.
findings.change: In ADR 0008 Context and in the index deferred row say 'the development sandbox of this repository, which is not managed by romeu'; add one deferred row: the product repository is developed inside a romeu-managed sandbox (dogfooding), until then the development sandbox's forwarded agent and token are as ADR 0008 measured, reopened by the v1.0.0 release or the first run of J1 on the maintainer's host; state in 06 6.4 that the rule governs sandboxes romeu renders.
findings.cost: Two clauses and one deferred row; no mechanism.

findings.defect: The signature row lists 'confirm-on-use where the agent supports it' as a mitigation although no probe measures it (A12 and B2 list keys), doctor cannot read it (the agent protocol does not expose the flag) and no kit or romeu setting controls it; and forwarding the signing key, which lets an agent sign in the operator's name on every commit, has no row with a trigger that reopens it, while ADR 0008's deferral covers the token only.
findings.scenario: An agent commits and signs work nobody asked for; the commits show Verified under the operator's key; the operator believed confirm-on-use was in place because the spec listed it; nothing in the spec says what event would make the forwarding be reconsidered.
findings.change: In 05 5.4 keep the one-key socket (06 6.4) as the control and either drop confirm-on-use or mark it 'not verifiable by romeu'; add a deferred row: a signing key per project or a non-forwarded signing path, until then the one-key socket, reopened by the first commit signed in the operator's name that the operator did not ask for, or a second contributor; let doctor print the key's comment and fingerprint so the operator can see which key is forwarded.
findings.cost: One row edit, one deferred row, one doctor output line.

findings.defect: romeu run step 3 starts sbx env run -d --clone <dir> and the spec never states what sbx reads from the workspace tree; if sbx honours a repository-local sandbox configuration, content an agent pushed to origin and the operator pulled into the host clone configures the sandbox outside gate 2, and no probe plants such a file (A5 covers the env file only).
findings.scenario: An agent commits a sandbox configuration file into the primary repository; the operator pulls the host clone by hand (05 5.4 row 1 allows it); the next romeu run creates a sandbox whose mounts or host commands came from the repository, not from sbxenv.yaml, and gate 2 saw nothing.
findings.change: Add to 11 A5: plant a repository-local sandbox configuration in the primary repo and record that sbx env plan and sbx env run read only the env file romeu names; state the result in 04 4.2 run step 3 and 03 3.3; if sbx does read such a file, add it to the I3 plant list and to the drift check or refuse it.
findings.cost: One probe step in T019, one sentence in two places; a guard only if the probe finds something.

findings.defect: romeu adopt records a sandbox gate 2 never saw as an open generation on a TTY confirmation that shows only the name and the workspace path, after which run, salvage and rm proceed (I26); boundary C says nothing unapproved is ever at a live path, and an adopted generation is unapproved, live, and reported only as 'recreate digest unknown'.
findings.scenario: After host state is lost (J3), the operator adopts a same-name sandbox that was created by hand or by an earlier env file with a read-write mount of $HOME; romeu run attaches, egress is reconciled, julieta runs; nothing told the operator what that sandbox mounts or which secrets it has.
findings.change: In 04 4.2 adopt: before the prompt print what sbx reports about the sandbox (mounts, policies, secrets, image) from sbx ls --json and sbx policy ls, escaped; in 01 1.6 and 05 5.4 state that an adopted generation is accepted as it stands until recreated, and let status say 'adopted, not gated' until then; record in A4 which fields sbx ls --json gives for this.
findings.cost: One A4 observation, one adopt output block, one 05 5.4 row, a status field.

findings.defect: internal/sbxdrv/** is 'the only code that runs sbx' (12 12.2) and holds the I4 (no --auto-approve) and I25 (no secret value forms) guards, yet it is on no ask-first surface, while internal/gitsafe/** is a surface for the same reason on the git side; plan.md question 28 saw the gap and took no plan change.
findings.scenario: A PR touching only sbxdrv adds a flag to the env run builder; no approval line is required, mutate does not run on it until the scheduled fuzz.yml, and the fake sbx's exit 99 is the only guard that notices, if the e2e reaches that builder.
findings.change: Add a surface in 05 5.3: id sbxdrv, globs internal/sbxdrv/**, reason: every sbx invocation on the host and the guards of I4 and I25.
findings.cost: Four lines in .github/ask-first.yaml and the regenerated CODEOWNERS.

findings.defect: ADR 0007's Threat model defers two escapes that act on go run before tools/ci starts (an untracked go.work, GOFLAGS such as -overlay) 'until the hook next changes, or until the sandbox-token question (Q25) is decided'; Q25 was decided on 2026-10-07 (ADR 0008), the trigger fired, the item is in no table and nothing reopened it, and it cites a plan.md deferral row that no longer exists.
findings.scenario: A deferral outside the one table whose trigger fires silently is the case ADR 0005 was written against; the maintainer's host hook (L2-1) runs go run on the tree, where both escapes act.
findings.change: Add the item to the index Deferred decisions with what holds (the hook runs go run on the tree as checked out) and a fresh trigger (the next change to .githooks/pre-push, or the first host run of tools/ci from a commit the maintainer did not read); add a one-line note to ADR 0007's Status or Consequences pointing at the row (a superseding note, not a rewrite).
findings.cost: One table row and one pointer line.

findings.defect: Memory directories and the spool are agent-writable host directories under $HOME/dev by default, and boundary D's 'no host tool is pointed at an agent-writable tree' is false for tools pointed at $HOME by default (Spotlight importers, Quick Look, Time Machine), which parse the files without the operator opening anything; the 05 5.4 row speaks only of an operator who opens the directory, and I24 forbids the dotfile that would exclude a memory dir from indexing.
findings.scenario: An agent writes a crafted document into memory/<dir>/entries/; mdworker parses it on the host within seconds; a parser defect in a host importer executes with the operator's user; romeu never read the file.
findings.change: In 02 2.3 have sync create <name>-env/.metadata_never_index (outside every mount, so I24 is untouched) and say why; add a doctor warning when the marker is missing or the root is inside a Time Machine or cloud-synced path; widen the 05 5.4 row to host indexers; reword boundary D to name what it checks.
findings.cost: One file written by sync, one doctor row, two sentences.

findings.defect: The 'Truth, in git' row names PR review as the control without the 05 5.4 caveat that ADR 0008 asked every leaning text to point at; the 'Agent output that reaches the host' row omits julieta's --json output that romeu parses and acts on (version, status, setup; the agent is root in the sandbox), the config repository's own blobs (specs, kits, locks), and the raw terminal bytes of the final exec; 02 2.6 still says memory is the only agent-written mount, before the spool existed.
findings.scenario: An implementer of pull trusts julieta status --json as if julieta were romeu's; a 32 MiB JSON document or a hostile field reaches a decoder with no cap stated, where every other agent input has one (I12, I24, I32).
findings.change: Turn the one row into a short table of host-side consumers of sandbox bytes with the verb per consumer (parsed with a schema and a cap, copied verbatim, fed to git, displayed escaped, executed raw), add the three missing rows, point the Truth row at 05 5.4, state in 04 4.2 that julieta's JSON is decoded strictly with a size cap, and fix 02 2.6; add I12, I17 and I28 to boundary A's list.
findings.cost: One table of about eight rows, two sentences.

findings.defect: Three claims are wider than their measurement: I23 'No host tool auto-trusts $ROMEU_ROOT' is tested over four tools; I30 'julieta runs only as delivered' and boundary C repeat it while 06 6.3 says the check proves compatibility, not integrity, and a root agent can bind-mount over the read-only path (A3 tests remount only); I2 and 04 4.2 cite 'the fixed set' of review-checkout hardening keys that no page lists.
findings.scenario: A reader cites I23 as a universal and adds a fifth host tool with auto-trust (a shell hook on cd) that doctor never sees; a reviewer treats I30 as a host control.
findings.change: Name the four tools in I23; retitle I30 to 'julieta is delivered read-only and checked for compatibility' and align boundary C with 06 6.3; list the review-checkout key set once in 05 5.1 and have I2 cite it.
findings.cost: Wording in three rows and one short list.

findings.defect: The doctor VS Code row checks trust disabled and $ROMEU_ROOT or a parent trusted; a single host clone or review checkout trusted by itself is not checked, while 05 5.4 rows 1 and 2 and J4 step 4 lean on Restricted Mode.
findings.scenario: The operator presses Trust on one review checkout to run a task; .vscode/tasks.json pushed by the agent runs on the host at the next open; doctor stays green.
findings.change: Add to the doctor table: any folder under $ROMEU_ROOT present in VS Code's trusted folders list fails (I23), pre.
findings.cost: One doctor row and fixture.

findings.defect: The salvage host half verifies and unbundles into the operator's host clone store without the git fsck --strict that pull runs on an unbundled head (04 4.2), although 05 5.1 says transfer.fsckObjects does not cover unbundle and the operator later runs plain git in that clone (05 5.4 row 1).
findings.scenario: A malformed object in a salvage bundle lands in the host clone's object store; it is harmless to romeu and reached by the operator's git log or gc later.
findings.change: Add to 08 8.5 host half step 2: git fsck --strict on each unbundled head, the call kit materialisation uses.
findings.cost: One sentence, one call.

findings.defect: sandboxOptions (cpus, memory) is the one spec field that reaches a host resource with no gate (untagged, recreate-class) and no bound in 03 3.1, so a merged hostile spec can claim the host's whole memory without a prompt.
findings.scenario: A spec sets memory to the host's total; recreate applies it; the host swaps; nothing asked.
findings.change: Either give cpus and memory a validation bound in 03 3.1 or add a 05 5.4 row naming the ungated host-resource field and why it is accepted.
findings.cost: One rule or one row.

findings.defect: Lock-derived artifact hosts are agent-chosen strings that end in an sbx policy allow network argv and the gate diff, and nothing says they pass the domain rule of 03 3.1 first; and no size cap is stated for the repository blobs romeu reads on the host at a pinned commit (projects/*.yaml, kit files, mise.lock), while every other agent input has one.
findings.scenario: A lock records an artifact URL whose host is a port literal or a leading-dash string; romeu builds an argv with it; or a multi-GiB mise.lock blob is read whole into romeu's memory on the host.
findings.change: State in 07 7.5 step 3 that lock hosts are validated by the 03 3.1 domain rule before use and refused otherwise; add a size cap per blob romeu reads from a repository (03 opening or I27) with the cap in one table.
findings.cost: Two sentences and one constant.

findings.defect: The threat model names 'issue and PR text, fetched pages and dependencies' as steering (ADR 0008) and not the product's own memory: a lesson entry and the latest handoff are printed into every later session by SessionStart (08 8.2) and survive recreate by design, and romeu handoff prints agent prose to the operator, the one path from agent text to a host action that escaping cannot stop.
findings.scenario: A compromised session writes a lesson entry with instructions; every later session of that repo reads it first; or the handoff tells the operator to run a command on the host and they do.
findings.change: Add to the 05 opening threat list 'persist instructions to a later session through memory' and to 05 5.4 one row each for memory as a steering channel (mitigation: the SessionStart print is labelled as agent text; romeu handoff prints a one-line banner that the text is the agent's) and for the persuasive handoff.
findings.cost: Two rows and one banner line.

findings.defect: Boundary B holds on the three paths the lens asks about (the gate diff shows argv by design and never a value, events have closed fields, run-timings carries two numbers), but the path the spec itself names, salvage with --include-transcripts and the agent/ state copy ('they may contain echoed tokens', step 5), brings secret values onto host disk into a memory dir whose file and directory modes 02 never states, unlike host settings (0600) and state (0700).
findings.scenario: The operator salvages with transcripts; a token echoed in a transcript sits in $HOME/dev/<name>-env/memory/<dir>/salvage/ with default modes, indexed and backed up (L2-12).
findings.change: State in 02 2.3 and 08 8.1 the modes sync creates memory dirs with (0700) and that julieta writes 0600; say in 08 8.5 that salvage payloads are treated as secret-bearing at rest; print the full field list of run-timings.v1 in 04 4.2 or point at the schema and say it holds durations only.
findings.cost: Three sentences.

findings.defect: Q13's default 'per-project fine-grained tokens, name@project' is a default the spec says it already follows, and ADR 0008 decision 3 says the token in every project is the operator's own; the open-question row and the decision record disagree on what holds today.
findings.scenario: A second adopter reads Q13, binds one token per project and believes projects are isolated on GitHub; the reference instance is not.
findings.change: In Q13's Default cell add 'the mechanism is per project; the reference instance binds the operator's own token in every project today (ADR 0008)'.
findings.cost: One clause.

findings.defect: 5.3 reads as if the maintainer's explicit approval were enforced ('need the maintainer's explicit approval'); as measured on 2026-10-08 the ruleset requires no review and the approval line is typed by the author (05 5.4), and ADR 0008 asked texts that lean on the review to point at 05 5.4, which 5.3 does not.
findings.scenario: A contributor reads 5.3 alone and believes a surface change cannot merge without the maintainer.
findings.change: Add one sentence to 5.3: what this approval is worth with one account is in 05 5.4.
findings.cost: One sentence.

findings.defect: Blocks O1, O3 and O6 and tasks T026 and T092 have the maintainer run the hook (go run ./tools/ci fast at main) in a plain host clone, the plan knows it ('a results-only branch runs main's own tools/ci through the hook') and asks for the diff of a resolution commit to be read, not the diff of main since the host last ran it; T001 to T003 are merged, so the window is open now.
findings.scenario: Between two sittings the token merges a change to tools/ci; at block O3 the maintainer pushes results through the hook and runs it unread.
findings.change: In each of O1, O3, O6, T026, T092 add: before enabling or running the hook, read git log -p <last host run>..main -- tools/ci .githooks mise.toml mise.lock go.mod in the plain clone, and record the commit read in the PR's Evidence; or run a released tools/ci; follows the rule L2-1 asks 10 10.2 to state.
findings.cost: One sentence in five places; the rule itself belongs to the spec.

findings.defect: Question 28 records that the I4, I25 and I8 guards live on no ask-first surface and takes 'no plan change'; the surface is a spec gap (L2-10) and the plan should carry the task that adds it rather than close the question.
findings.scenario: T029 lands sbxdrv with no approval line and mutate does not run on its PR.
findings.change: Change question 28's reading to: 05 5.3 gains a sbxdrv surface, added in T003's follow-up before T029; mark T029 Ask-first: sbxdrv.
findings.cost: Two lines in the plan.

postmortem: It is some months after v1.0.0 and the product failed the way I have seen hosts fall: not through the window the spec barred but through the door it left as a working agreement. (1) The host fell through the repository's own tooling: romeu never executed an agent's byte; the maintainer's host did, every push, through the tracked pre-push hook (12 12.4) running agent-written tools/ci merged to main by a token the sandbox holds (ADR 0008, 05 5.4); the control was written once for the bootstrap (10 10.2) and the plan asked for a resolution commit's diff, not main's (O3, O6). Crosses index Boundaries, 01 1.3 A, 05 5.4, 10 10.2, 12 12.4, ADR 0008. (2) The release nobody signed was the one everybody installed: a v* tag pushed by the token ran release.yml, CI wrote checksums.txt, GitHub attested, and J1 step 2 verified exactly those two things; the operator-held signing credential (05 5.4 Release signing, ADR 0008 decision 6) had no consumer, and the 'reviewed, signed, attested' release of the threat model (05 opening) was trusted because the operator believed it was. Crosses 05 opening, 05 5.4, S1, 09 J1, 11 B1, 10 10.2. (3) The release workflow needed what the grammar forbade (read-or-none permissions, no tokens, 10 10.2) and the PR that landed it widened the grammar under pressure with an author-typed approval line. Crosses 10 10.2, 12 12.10, index Deferred decisions. (4) The gate reviewed shell at a prompt and nobody knew where it ran: gate 2 showed personal-kit install steps and lifecycle hooks (01 1.4, 06 6.1), the operator pressed y on a 10 000-line diff with the summary repeated above the prompt as designed (I29), and no probe had asked where the step executes (11 A11, A14). (5) Every project had the operator's whole account (Q13 as written versus ADR 0008 decision 3): a shop agent merged a spec into verona (01 1.2 'PR review'), added its own repository, the next sync cloned it behind a gate that showed a github.com URL, the operator trusted that one folder in VS Code and doctor had no row for a single trusted folder (04 4.2, I23). (6) Commits Verified in the operator's name and no one could tell: one key, reachable on every sbx call (04 4.1, 06 6.4), confirm-on-use in a mitigation cell nobody could verify (05 5.4, 11 A12), the security log's coverage never checked (ADR 0008 decision 5), the 2-session trigger with no counter (13). (7) The product's own development never ran under the product's rules: two forwarded keys (ADR 0008 Context) against 06 6.4's one, and no row saying when dogfooding begins. (8) The things we did not say out loud: review was a second agent most days and the ruleset required none (12 12.9, 10 10.2 item a); adopt put an ungated sandbox under management on a name and a path (01 1.6); Spotlight indexed every memory dir under $HOME/dev on day one (02 2.3, 05 5.4); a lesson entry from one compromised session was printed into every later session (08 8.1, 8.2); the ADR 0007 deferral whose trigger was Q25 fired on 2026-10-07 and nothing moved; the ledger told us what failed inside sandboxes (13) and nothing told us what the host did with sandbox bytes, so detection came from outside, as it did last time. What would have held: not more invariants in romeu, those held; a sentence for the maintainer's host equal to the one for romeu with a control and a record, a consumer for the operator's release signature, a measured answer to where a kit step runs, and the product's own sandbox under the product's rules with a date.
lens_critique: This lens treats 'agent bytes are data on the host' as the whole of success and would accept a product nobody can operate; it prices every convenience as an incident and would demand mechanisms where this product, built by one maintainer, has correctly chosen a human checkpoint and said so (ADR 0008's 'process only' is a decision, not an oversight, and the lens's instinct is to refuse it rather than make its radius and control explicit). It looks from the host inward and is nearly blind to what happens inside the sandbox, where this product's users lose work and are steered, and it undervalues availability (a host that swaps is a failure too). It also over-weights the macOS host as the crown jewel when, for the operator, the GitHub account's reach is already the larger asset and the spec treats it as such. Its definition of success is right for romeu's runtime and too narrow for a product whose development process is part of its trust chain.
missing_viewpoint: The adversary who starts inside the sandbox: a red-teamer who is root in the microVM with the operator's token, the signing socket and a memory dir, and asks what to do next. L2 looks from the host inward, L5 plays the cooperative agent, L7 looks at the supply chain, L16 at the data; nobody plays the hostile agent whose first move is to steer the next session through a lesson entry, merge its own PR, or tag a release, and nobody therefore traces an attack from inside out across pages the way an attacker would.
